title: Configure and Customize a Nodics Application
readerIntent: Place an application setting at the correct layer and verify it safely.
priorKnowledge: Know the owning capability and the runtime scope that must vary.
owner: Owning capability plus Nodics configuration contracts
summary: Start with the owning module default, override only at the required application or runtime scope, and validate both expected and fallback behavior.

sections.heading: Example decision
paragraphs: Suppose a customer project needs a shorter cache lifetime in local development than in production. The cache capability owns the property name and safe default. The project changes the value in the relevant layered properties.js configuration; it does not copy the cache service or place application behavior in package.json.

sections.heading: Implementation steps
items: Find the capability that owns the behavior and confirm an existing property or extension contract.
Check all existing loaders and override paths before proposing another configuration mechanism.
Keep standard package metadata in package.json and application behavior in properties.js or an explicit runtime-governance contract.
Place secrets in the deployment secret mechanism, never committed source.
Override at the narrowest correct scope and document the default, allowed values, units, restart behavior, and security implications.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Default value when no override exists.
Expected value at the selected environment and topology.
No leakage into another environment, server, node, tenant, or customer.
Invalid type, range, missing dependency, and secret-handling behavior.
Restart and governed runtime-update behavior where supported.
Regression of the original reusable default.
